title: Background music, round 6: new YuE2 pieces in the opening theme's style
context: Round 6 of the background music, the direction you picked in music-direction-1: new YuE2 instrumentals in the opening theme's style. Nobody has listened to these before you. I can't hear audio, so I only checked them by measurement.

Same model as the opening theme (YuE2, run locally, no cost) and the opening's style tags (anime J-pop, melodic bass, sparkling synths, catchy melody), minus the vocal ones. Each piece is a new piece, not a variation of the opening's melody, with its own band and mood. The opening was sung; to keep these instrumental I used the instrumental add-on for YuE2, which needs the full-precision model, so the sound may differ a little from the opening.

Your notes so far: round 5's title was "too slow and somber", its day piece "almost jamaican", and they "all still fall short of the current"; round 4 sounded like "an epic ballad" and was "too similar". So these are livelier (104 to 140 BPM), with no strings or orchestra, and each use has a different band.

Five pieces, one each for the title menu, outdoors during the day, the evening, the office and the shop street. Each card's note says where it would play and what plays there today. Each card is the loop the game would play (1:49 to 2:21), then the first 15 seconds of the repeat so you can hear the loop point. For comparison, the opening theme and today's calm loop are at the top.

I made ten pieces, two per use, and kept the one per use that measured best. The five I left out stay on this machine: title-2: title-1 (same tags) is in a major key and its loop point matches better; title-2 came out in F# minor.; day-2: Demucs found singing in it: the vocal stem is -3.3 dB of the mix, in 42% of the piece.; evening-2: its loop point has an 18 dB jump in level.; office-1: no good loop point (match 0.58; the cut-off is 0.45).; shops-2: came out in Ab minor, which reads less playful than shops-1.

Nothing here is in the game yet. Pick the ones that fit and reject the rest, and say what is wrong with any you reject. What happens next: your picks replace the current loops in those places in the game; for any use you reject, I make a new round for just that use with your notes; your round-5 fallbacks (evening-2, office-2, shops-1) stay available if nothing here is better.
